nodes.name: Energy maximization problem defining the PSWFs
nodes.statement: We first recall that for $c>0$, the classical prolate spheroidal wave functions (PSWFs) were first discovered and studied by D. Slepian and his co-authors, see \cite{Slepian1, Slepian2}. These PSWFs are defined as the solutions of the following energy maximization problem : \begin{equation*} \mbox{ Find } g=\arg\max_{f\in B_c}\frac{\int_{-1}^1|f(t)|^2 dt}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(t)|^2 dt} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Find the $B_c$-bandlimited function maximizing the fraction of its energy concentrated on $[-1,1]$.

nodes.name: Classical Paley-Winer space $B_c$
nodes.statement: Where $B_c$ is the classical Paley-Winer space, defined by \begin{equation} B_c=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c]\}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Fourier transform $\widehat f$ on $L^2(\mathbb R)$
nodes.statement: Here, $\widehat f$ is the Fourier transform of $f\in L^2(\mathbb R),$ defined by ${\displaystyle \widehat f(\xi)=\lim_{A\rightarrow +\infty}\int_{[-A,A]} e^{-i x\xi} f(x)\, dx.}$
nodes.definiendum: $\widehat f$, the Fourier transform of $f\in L^2(\mathbb R)$

nodes.name: Slepian's characterization of the PSWFs as eigenfunctions of $\mathcal Q_c$ and $\mathcal L_c$
nodes.statement: Moreover, it has been shown in \cite{Slepian1}, that the PSWFs are also the eigenfunctions of the integral operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c}$ defined on $L^2(-1,1)$ by $${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 \frac{\sin(c(x-y))}{\pi(x-y)} f(y)\, dy} $$ as well as the eigenfunctions of a commuting differential operator $ \mathcal{L}_c$ with $ \mathcal{Q}_c$ and given by $$ \mathcal L_c f(x)= (1-x^2)f''(x)-2x f'(x) - c^2 x^2 f(x) $$
nodes.statement_short: The PSWFs are simultaneously the eigenfunctions of the sinc-kernel operator $\mathcal Q_c$ and of the commuting differential operator $\mathcal L_c$.
assumptions: for $c>0$, the classical prolate spheroidal wave functions (PSWFs)
conclusions: the PSWFs are also the eigenfunctions of the integral operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c}$ defined on $L^2(-1,1)$ by $${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 \frac{\sin(c(x-y))}{\pi(x-y)} f(y)\, dy} $$
as well as the eigenfunctions of a commuting differential operator $ \mathcal{L}_c$ with $ \mathcal{Q}_c$ and given by $$ \mathcal L_c f(x)= (1-x^2)f''(x)-2x f'(x) - c^2 x^2 f(x) $$

nodes.name: Generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs)
nodes.statement: In this paper, we are interested in a weighted family of PSWFs called the generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs), recently given in \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} and\cite{Wang2} . They are defined as the eigenfunctions of the Gegenbauer perturbed differential operator, \begin{equation*} \mathcal L^{(\alpha)}_c \varphi(x)= (1-x^2)\varphi''(x)-2\left(\alpha+1\right)x\varphi'(x) - c^2 x^2 \varphi(x)= \mathcal L_0 \varphi(x)-c^2 x^2 \varphi(x), \mbox{ where } \alpha>-1; c>0, \end{equation*} as well as the eigenfunctions of the following commuting weighted finite Fourier transform integral operator, \begin{equation} {\displaystyle \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,(1-y^2)^{\alpha}\, dy,\, \alpha > -1.} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The GPSWFs are the eigenfunctions of the Gegenbauer-perturbed operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$, equivalently of the commuting weighted finite Fourier transform $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$.

nodes.name: Convergence rate of the GPSWFs projection in the weighted Sobolev space $H^s_{\alpha}$
nodes.statement: Let $c>1$ and $\alpha >0$, then there exist constants $K>0$ and $a>0$ such that, when $N > m_{\alpha}c$ with $m_{\alpha}=4.13\left(1.28+\frac{2\alpha+1}{1.9}\right)^{0.55}$ and $f \in H^s_{\alpha}$; $s > 0$, we have the inequality \begin{eqnarray} \|f-S_N(f)\|_{L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha})} &\leq& \left(1+ \left(\frac{N}{2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-s}{2}} \|f\|_{H^s_{\alpha}} +K.e^{-a N}\|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} \end{eqnarray} Where $S_N(f)(t)=\ds{\sum_{n<N}}<f,\psi_{n,c}^{\alpha}>_{L^2_{\alpha}(I)}\psi_{n,c}^{\alpha}$
nodes.statement_short: For $N$ past $m_\alpha c$, the GPSWFs truncation error in $L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)$ splits into an algebraic $N^{-s}$ term plus an exponentially small term.

nodes.name: Super-exponential decay of the singular values $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ (announced)
nodes.statement: For given real numbers $c > 0$,$ \;\; \;\alpha\geq 0$ and for any integer $n > \frac{ec+1}{2},$ we have \begin{equation} | \mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)| \leq \frac{k_{\alpha}}{c^{\frac{\alpha}{2}+1}\log\left(\frac{2n-1}{ec}\right)} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}},\;\;\; k_{\alpha}=\left(\frac{2}{e}\right)^{1+\frac{\alpha}{2}}\pi(\Gamma(\alpha+1))^{1/2}. \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq \frac{K_\alpha}{c^{\alpha+1}\log^2(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}\Big(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\Big)^{2n+\alpha} \quad \mbox{with} \quad K_{\alpha} = \frac{\pi}{2}\big(2/e \big)^{\alpha+2} \Gamma(\alpha+1)\nonumber \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Announced in the introduction: explicit super-exponentially decaying bounds on $|\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ for $n>(ec+1)/2$.

nodes.name: Weighted finite Fourier transform operator $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: The GPSWFs are defined as the eigenfunctions of the weighted finite Fourier transform operator $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)},$ defined by \begin{equation} \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f(x)=\int_{-1}^1 e^{icxy} f(y)\,\omega_{\alpha}(y)\, dy,\quad \omega_{\alpha}(y)=(1-y^2)^{\alpha},\quad \alpha >0 \end{equation}
nodes.definiendum: weighted finite Fourier transform operator $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$

nodes.name: Operator $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}=\frac{c}{2\pi}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)^*}\circ\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: They are also the eigenfunctions of the operator ${\displaystyle \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}=\frac{c}{2\pi}\mathcal F_c^{({\alpha})^*} \circ \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}},$ defined on $L^2{(I, \omega_{\alpha})}$ by \begin{equation} \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)} g (x) = \int_{-1}^1 \frac{c}{2 \pi}\mathcal K_{\alpha}(c(x-y)) g(y) \omega_{\alpha}(y) \, dy, \quad \mathcal K_{\alpha}(x)=\sqrt{\pi} 2^{\alpha+1/2}\Gamma(\alpha+1) \frac{J_{\alpha+1/2}(x)}{x^{\alpha+1/2}}. \end{equation} Here $ J_{\alpha}(\cdot)$ is the Bessel function of the first kind and order $ \alpha>-1.$
nodes.statement_short: The self-adjoint concentration operator on $L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)$ with Bessel-type kernel $\mathcal K_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Relation between the eigenvalues $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$
nodes.statement: Moreover, the eigenvalues $\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$ and $\mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$ are related to each others by the identity ${\displaystyle \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)= \frac{c}{2\pi } |\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|^2}.$

nodes.name: Gegenbauer-type Sturm-Liouville operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: Note that the previous two integral operators commute with the following Gegenbauer-type Sturm-Liouville operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)},$ defined by $$ \mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)} (f)(x)= -\frac{1}{\omega_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{d}{dx}\left[ \omega_{\alpha}(x) (1-x^2) f'(x)\right] +c^2 x^2 f(x),\quad \omega_{\alpha}(x)= (1-x^2)^{\alpha}.$$

nodes.name: Classical bounds on the eigenvalues $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$ of $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: Also, note that the $(n+1)-$th eigenvalue $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$ of $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ satisfies the following classical inequalities, \begin{equation} n (n+2\alpha+1) \leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \leq n (n+2\alpha+1) +c^2,\quad \forall n\geq 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: The GPSWFs $(\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)})_{n\geq 0}$
nodes.statement: We will denote by$(\ps)_{n\geq 0},$ the set of the eigenfunctions of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}, \mathcal Q_c^{(\alpha)}$ and $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}.$ They are called generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions (GPSWFs).

nodes.name: The GPSWFs form an orthogonal basis of $L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})$
nodes.statement: It has been shown that $ \{ \ps , n\geq 0 \} $ is an orthogonal basis of $ L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}), I=[-1,1].$
conclusions: $ \{ \ps , n\geq 0 \} $ is an orthogonal basis of $ L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}), I=[-1,1].$

nodes.name: Restricted Paley-Wiener space $B_c^{(\alpha)}$ of weighted $c$-band-limited functions
nodes.statement: We recall that the restricted Paley-Wiener space of weighted $c-$band-limited functions has been defined in \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} by \begin{equation} B_c^{(\alpha)}=\{ f\in L^2(\mathbb R),\,\, \mbox{Support } \widehat f\subseteq [-c,c],\, \, \widehat f\in L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)\}. \end{equation} Here, $L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)$ is the weighted $L^2(-c,c)-$space with norm given by $$\| f\|^2_{L^2\big((-c,c), \omega_{- \alpha}(\frac{\cdot}{c})\big)}= \int_{-c}^c |f(t)|^2 \omega_{-\alpha}\left(\frac{t}{c}\right)\, dt.$$
nodes.statement_short: The $c$-bandlimited functions whose Fourier transform additionally lies in the $\omega_{-\alpha}$-weighted $L^2(-c,c)$.
nodes.definiendum: restricted Paley-Wiener space of weighted $c-$band-limited functions

nodes.name: Super-exponential asymptotic decay of $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$
nodes.statement: It has been shown in \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} that the eigenvalues $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ decay asymptotically at a super-exponential rate that is for $ 0<b<4/e$ there exists $N_b \in \mathbb{N}$ such that : \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) < e^{-2n \log(\frac{bn}{c})} \qquad \forall n \geq N_b, \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For every $0<b<4/e$ the eigenvalues eventually satisfy $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)<e^{-2n\log(bn/c)}$.

nodes.name: Second decay rate of $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ for $0<\alpha<3/2$
nodes.statement: Note that a second decay rate of the $ \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ and valid for $0<\alpha <\frac{3}{2},$ has been recently given in \cite{Karoui-Souabni2}. More precisely, it has been shown in \cite{Karoui-Souabni2}, that if $c>0$ and $0<\alpha <\frac{3}{2}$, then there exist $N_{\alpha}(c)\in \mathbb N$ and a constant $C_{\alpha}>0$ such that \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq C_{\alpha} \exp\left(-(2n+1)\left[ \log\left(\frac{4n+4\alpha+2}{e c}\right)+ C_{\alpha} \frac{c^2}{2n+1}\right]\right),\quad \forall\, n\geq N_{\alpha}(c). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A sharper but restricted decay estimate, valid only for $0<\alpha<3/2$ and $n$ beyond $N_\alpha(c)$.

nodes.name: Normalized Jacobi polynomials $\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k$ and the Jacobi expansion of the GPSWFs
nodes.statement: In \cite{Karoui-Souabni1}, the authors have proposed the following scheme for the computation of the GPSWFs. In fact, since $\psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}\in L^2(I, \omega_{\alpha}),$ then its series expansion with respect to the Jacobi polynomials basis is given by \begin{equation} \psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}(x) =\sum_{k\geq 0} \beta_k^n \wJ_k (x),\quad x\in [-1,1]. \end{equation} Here, $\wJ_k$ denotes the normalized Jacobi polynomial of degree $k,$ given by \begin{equation} \wJ_{k}(x)= \frac{1}{\sqrt{h_k}}\J_k(x),\quad h_k=\frac{2^{2\alpha+1}\Gamma^2(k+\alpha+1)}{k!(2k+2\alpha+1)\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Expansion $\psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}=\sum_k \beta_k^n\widetilde P^{(\alpha,\alpha)}_k$ with the normalizing constants $h_k$.

nodes.name: Eigensystem for the expansion coefficients $\beta_k^n$ and eigenvalues $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$
nodes.statement: The expansion coefficients $\beta_k^n$ as well as the eigenvalues $\chi_n^\alpha(c)$ this system is given by \begin{eqnarray} \lefteqn{\frac{\sqrt{(k+1)(k+2)(k+2\alpha+1)(k+2\alpha+2)}}{(2k+2\alpha+3)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+5)(2k+2\alpha +1)}} c^2 \beta_{k+2}^n + \big( k(k+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \frac{2k(k+2\alpha+1)+2\alpha-1}{(2k+2\alpha+3)(2k+2\alpha-1)} \big) \beta_k^n}\nonumber \\ &&\hspace*{2cm} + \frac{\sqrt{k(k-1)(k+2\alpha)(k+2\alpha-1)}}{(2k+2\alpha-1)\sqrt{(2k+2\alpha+1)(2k+2\alpha-3)}} c^2 \beta_{k-2}^n= \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \beta_k^n, \quad k\geq 0. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: The five-term (tridiagonal in even/odd blocks) recurrence whose eigenpairs give $\beta^n$ and $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$.

nodes.name: Jacobi-weighted Sobolev space $H^r_{\alpha}(I)$
nodes.statement:
We denote, for any $ r \in \N $, $H^r_{\alpha}(I)$ the Jacobi-weighted Sobolev space by : $$ H^r_{\alpha}(I) = \{f \in L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}) : 
orm{f}_{\alpha,r}<\infty \} \quad \mbox{where} \quad 
orm{f}_{\alpha,r} = \displaystyle{\sum_{k=0}^r 
orm{f^{(k)}}_{\omega}^2} $$ In particular, $ L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}) = H^0_{\alpha}(I) $ and $ 
orm{.}_{\alpha,0} = 
orm{.}_{\omega} $. \ For any real r, we define the weighted Sobolev space $H^r_{\alpha}$ by interpolation $ H^r_{\alpha} = \Big[H^{[r]}_{\alpha},H^{[r]+1}_{\alpha}\Big]$ as it is done in \cite{Bergh-Lofstrom} and \cite{Bernardi-Maday}
nodes.statement_short: The $\omega_\alpha$-weighted Sobolev scale, extended to real $r$ by interpolation.

nodes.name: The space $H_0^s(I)$
nodes.statement: We denote by $ \mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I) $ the set of infinitely differentiable functions defined on $ I $. Let $H_0^s(I) $ be the completion of $ \mathcal{C}_{\infty}(I) $ in $H^s(I)$. $H_0^s(I) $ is a Hilbert space under the inner product. For $s\geq 0$, we define $H_0^s(I) $by interpolation as in \cite{Bergh-Lofstrom} and \cite{Bernardi-Maday}. \\

nodes.name: Super-exponential decay rate of the eigenvalues of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: For given real numbers $c > 0$,$ \;\; \;\alpha\geq 0$ and for any integer $n > \frac{ec+1}{2},$ we have \begin{equation} | \mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)| \leq \frac{k_{\alpha}}{c^{\frac{\alpha}{2}+1}\log\left(\frac{2n-1}{ec}\right)} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}},\;\;\; k_{\alpha}=\left(\frac{2}{e}\right)^{1+\frac{\alpha}{2}}\pi(\Gamma(\alpha+1))^{1/2}. \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c) \leq \frac{K_\alpha}{c^{\alpha+1}\log^2(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}\Big(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\Big)^{2n+\alpha} \quad \mbox{with} \quad K_{\alpha} = \frac{\pi}{2}\big(2/e \big)^{\alpha+2} \Gamma(\alpha+1) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit non-asymptotic bounds showing $|\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|$ and $\lambda_n^{(\alpha)}(c)$ decay super-exponentially once $n>(ec+1)/2$.

nodes.name: Proof of the super-exponential eigenvalue decay theorem
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Courant-Fischer-Weyl min-max principle on the span of normalized Jacobi polynomials, bound $\|\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}\widetilde P_k\|$ via Bessel and Gamma inequalities, then compare the tail sum with its integral.

nodes.name: Recall the Courant-Fischer-Weyl min-max principle
nodes.statement: We first recall the Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle concerning the eigenvalues of a compact self-adjoint operator $T$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal G,$ with positive eigenvalues arranged in the decreasing order $\lambda_0\geq \lambda_1\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_n\geq \cdots ,$ then we have $$\lambda_n = \min_{f\in S_n}\,\,\, \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\|f\|_{\mathcal G}=1} < Tf, f>_{\mathcal G},$$
nodes.statement_short: Recall the min-max variational characterization of the eigenvalues of a compact self-adjoint operator.

nodes.name: Specialize $T$, $\mathcal G$, $S_n$ and the test function $f$
nodes.statement: where $S_n$ is a subspace of $\mathcal G$ of dimension $n.$ In our case, we have $T=\mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)},$ $\mathcal G= L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}).$ We consider the special case of $$S_n=\mbox{Span}\left\{\wJ_0, \wJ_1,\ldots,\wJ_{n-1}\right\}$$ and $$f=\ds\sum_{k\geq n} a_k \wJ_k \in S_n^{\perp},\qquad \parallel f\parallel_{L^2_{(I,\omega_\alpha)}}=\ds\sum_{k\geq n}|a_k|^2=1.$$ Here the $ \wJ_{k} $ are the normalized Jacobi polynomials given by \eqref{JacobiP}.
nodes.statement_short: Take $T=\mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}$ and $S_n$ the span of the first $n$ normalized Jacobi polynomials.

nodes.name: Recall the Bessel representation of $\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}P_k$ and the moment bound
nodes.statement: From [\cite{NIST} page 456], we have \begin{equation} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \J_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} = \parallel \sqrt{\pi} \left(\frac{2}{cx}\right) ^{\alpha+1/2} \frac{\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\Gamma(k+1)}J_{k+\alpha+1/2}(cx) \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}. \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \parallel x^k \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}^2=\beta(k+1/2,\alpha+1)\leq \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{e}}\frac{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}{k^{\alpha+1}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Import from NIST the closed form of $\|\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}P_k\|$ and the Beta-function bound on $\|x^k\|$.

nodes.name: Apply the classical bound on the Bessel function
nodes.statement: By using the well-known bound of the Bessel function given by \begin{equation} |J_{\alpha}(x)|\leq \frac{|x|^{\alpha}}{2^{\alpha}\Gamma(\alpha+1)}\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\forall\alpha>-1/2, \;\; \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, \end{equation} one gets, \begin{eqnarray} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \wJ_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\sqrt{h_k}\Gamma(k+1)\Gamma(k+\alpha+3/2)}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k} \parallel x^k \parallel_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}. \nonumber\\ &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\Gamma(k+\alpha+1)}{\sqrt{h_k}\Gamma(k+1)\Gamma(k+\alpha+3/2)}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k}\left(\frac{\pi}{e}\right)^{1/4}\frac{\sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Insert $|J_\alpha(x)|\leq |x|^\alpha/(2^\alpha\Gamma(\alpha+1))$ to bound $\|\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}\widetilde P_k\|$.

nodes.name: Apply Batir's Gamma-function inequalities
nodes.statement: Next, we use \eqref{JacobiP} and the following useful inequalities for the Gamma function, see \cite{Batir} \begin{equation} \sqrt{2e}\left(\frac{x+1/2}{e}\right)^{x+1/2}\leq\Gamma(x+1)\leq \sqrt{2\pi}\left(\frac{x+1/2}{e}\right)^{x+1/2}\;,\;\;\; x>0. \end{equation} Then, we have \begin{eqnarray} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \wJ_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq & \frac{\sqrt{\pi}\sqrt{(k+\alpha+\frac{1}{2})\Gamma(k+2\alpha+1)}}{2^{\alpha+\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{\Gamma(k+1)}\Gamma(k+\alpha+\frac{3}{2})}\left(\frac{c}{2}\right) ^{k}\left(\frac{\pi}{e}\right)^{\frac{1}{4}}\frac{\sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}\big(k+2\alpha+\frac{1}{2}\Big)^{\frac{k}{2}+\alpha+\frac{1}{4 }}}{\sqrt{ec}2^{\alpha}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}\left(k+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{k}{2}+\frac{1}{4}}\left(k+\alpha+1\right)^{k+\alpha+\frac{1}{2}}} \left(\frac{ce}{2}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2 }}\nonumber\\ &=&\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}2^{\alpha}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\left(1+\frac{\alpha-\frac{1}{2}}{k+\alpha+1}\right)^{\frac{k}{2}+\alpha+\frac{1}{4}} \left(\frac{ce}{2k+1}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2}}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Replace the Gamma factors by Batir's two-sided estimates and simplify the resulting product.

nodes.name: Discard the decreasing factor $g_a$
nodes.statement: Since the function $g_a(x)=\left(1+\frac{a}{x}\right)^{a+x}$ for $x\geq1$ and $a>-1$ is decreasing on $[1,+\infty[$. Then, we have \begin{eqnarray} \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \wJ_k\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} &\leq &\frac{\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{c}k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \left(\frac{ce}{2k+1}\right) ^{k+\frac{1}{2}}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Use monotonicity of $g_a(x)=(1+a/x)^{a+x}$ to drop it and obtain the clean bound $(ce/(2k+1))^{k+1/2}$.

nodes.name: Bound the quadratic form by Hölder and Minkowski
nodes.statement: Hence, For the previous $f\in S_n^{\perp},$ and by using H\"older's inequality, combined with the Minkowski's inequality for an infinite sums, and taking into account that $\|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}= 1,$ so that $|a_k|\leq 1,$ for $k\geq n,$ one gets: \begin{eqnarray} |< \mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f,f>_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}|&=&|< \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f,\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}f>_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}| \leq \sum_{k\geq n} |a_k|^2 \| \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} \wJ_k\|^2_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}\\ &\leq&\left(\frac{2^\frac{1}{4}\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}} \sum_{k\geq n} \left(\frac{ec}{2k+1}\right)^{k+1/2}\frac{1}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\right)^2 \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: For unit $f\in S_n^{\perp}$, bound $|\langle \mathcal F_c^{\alpha^*}\mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)}f,f\rangle|$ by the squared tail sum.

nodes.name: Compare the tail sum with its integral counterpart
nodes.statement: The decay of the sequence appearing in the previous sum, allows us to compare this later with its integral counterpart, that is \begin{equation} \sum_{k\geq n} \left(\frac{ec}{2k+1}\right)^{k+1/2}\frac{1}{k^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}} \leq \int_{n-1}^{\infty}\frac{ e^{-(x+1/2) \log(\frac{2x+1}{ec})}}{x^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\, dx\leq \int_{n-1}^{\infty}\frac{ e^{-(x+1/2)\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})}}{(n-1)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\, dx. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\sum_{k\geq n}$ by an integral from $n-1$, producing the $1/\log((2n-1)/ec)$ factor.

nodes.name: Combine the estimates and conclude by min-max
nodes.statement: Hence, by using (\ref{Eq3.3}) and (\ref{Eq3.4}), one concludes that \begin{eqnarray} \max_{f\in S_n^{\perp},\, \|f\|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})=1}} < \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f, \mathcal F_c^{(\alpha)} f>^{1/2}_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})}&\leq &\frac{2^\frac{1}{4}\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)}}{\sqrt{ec}} \frac{1}{\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n-1/2}\frac{1}{(n-1)^{\frac{\alpha+1}{2}}}\nonumber\\ &\leq&\pi \sqrt{\Gamma(\alpha+1)} \left(\frac{2}{ec}\right)^{\frac{\alpha+2}{2}} \frac{1}{\log(\frac{2n-1}{ec})} \left(\frac{ec}{2n-1}\right)^{n+\frac{\alpha}{2}} \end{eqnarray} To conclude the proof of the theorem, it suffices to use the Courant-Fischer-Weyl Min-Max variational principle.$\qquad \Box $
nodes.statement_short: Combine the tail bound with the min-max principle to obtain the stated bound on $|\mu_n^{(\alpha)}(c)|$.

nodes.name: Remark on the improvement over the previously known decay rates
nodes.statement: The decay rate given by the last proposition improve the two results mentioned above \eqref{decaylambda0} and \eqref{decay_lambda2}. Indeed, we have a more precise result furthermore the proof given in \cite{Karoui-Souabni2} contains two serious drawbacks. It is only valid in the particular case $0 < \alpha < 3/2 $ and clearly more sophisticated than the previous one.
nodes.statement_short: The new bound is more precise and, unlike Karoui-Souabni 2017, is not restricted to $0<\alpha<3/2$.

nodes.name: Sturm-Liouville ODE satisfied by the GPSWFs
nodes.statement: For this purpose, we first recall that $\ps $ are the bounded solutions of the following ODE : \begin{equation} \omega_{\alpha}(x)\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)} \psi(x)+w_{\alpha}(x)\chi_{n,\alpha}\psi(x)= ( w_{\alpha}(x)\psi'(x)(1-x^2))'+ w_{\alpha}(x)(\chi_{n}^{\alpha}-c^2 x^2)\psi(x)=0,\quad x\in [-1,1]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The GPSWFs are the bounded solutions on $[-1,1]$ of the weighted second-order ODE with eigenvalue $\chi_n^{\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Incomplete elliptic integral $S(x)$
nodes.statement: As it is done in \cite{Bonami-Karoui2}, we consider the incomplete elliptic integral \begin{equation} S(x)=\int_x^1 \sqrt{\frac{1-qt^2}{1-t^2}}\, dt,\qquad q=\frac{c^2}{\chi_n^\alpha(c)}<1. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Liouville-type transform $\psi(x)=\phi_{\alpha}(x)V(S(x))$
nodes.statement: Then, we write $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ into the form \begin{equation} \psi(x)=\phi_{\alpha}(x)V(S(x)),\qquad \phi_{\alpha}(x)=(1-x^2)^{(-1-2\alpha)/4} (1-qx^2)^{-1/4}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Second-order ODE satisfied by $V$
nodes.statement: By combining (\ref{eq2_diff}), (\ref{Liouvile_transform2}) and using straightforward computations, it can be easily checked that $V(\cdot)$ satisfies the following second order differential equation \begin{equation} V''(s)+\left(\chi_{n,\alpha}+\theta_{\alpha}(s)\right)V(s)=0,\quad s\in [0, S(0)] \end{equation} with $$ \theta_{\alpha}(S(x))=(w_{\alpha}(x)(1-x^2)\phi_{\alpha}'(x))'\frac{1}{\phi_{\alpha}(x)w_{\alpha}(x)(1-qx^2)}.$$
nodes.statement_short: After the Liouville transform, $V$ solves $V''+(\chi_{n,\alpha}+\theta_{\alpha})V=0$ on $[0,S(0)]$.
assumptions: By combining (\ref{eq2_diff}), (\ref{Liouvile_transform2}) and using straightforward computations,

nodes.name: Auxiliary function $Q_{\alpha}(x)$
nodes.statement: Define $ Q_{\alpha}(x)=w_{\alpha}(x)^2(1-x^2)(1-qx^2),$ then we have ${\displaystyle \frac{\phi_{\alpha}'(x)}{\phi_{\alpha}(x)}=-1/4 \frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}. }$

nodes.name: Explicit expression of $\theta_{\alpha}(S(x))$
nodes.statement: It follows that $\theta_{\alpha}(s)$ can be written as \begin{equation} \theta_{\alpha}(S(x))=\frac{1}{16(1-qx^2)}\Big[\Big(\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)^2(1-x^2)-4\frac{d}{dx}\Big((1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}\Big)-4(1-x^2)\frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\Big]. \end{equation} Since $ Q_{\alpha}(x)=w_{\alpha}^2(x)Q_0(x),$ then we have ${\displaystyle \frac{Q_{\alpha}'(x)}{Q_{\alpha}(x)}=2\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}+\frac{Q_0'(x)}{Q_0(x)}} $ and ${\displaystyle \frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}=-\frac{2\alpha x}{1-x^2}.} $ Hence, we have \begin{eqnarray} \theta_{\alpha}(S(x)) &=&\theta_0(S(x))+\frac{-1}{4(1-qx^2)}\Big[ \big(\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}\big)^2 (1-x^2)+2\frac{d}{dx}[(1-x^2)\frac{w_{\alpha}'(x)}{w_{\alpha}(x)}] \Big] \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{1}{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\Big( -\alpha^2 x^2 + \alpha (1-x^2) \Big) \nonumber \\ &=&\theta_0(S(x))+ \frac{\alpha(1+\alpha)}{(1-qx^2)}-\frac{\alpha^2}{(1-q x^2)(1-x^2)}. \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: $\theta_\alpha$ equals $\theta_0$ plus two explicit rational corrections in $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\theta_{\alpha}\circ S$
nodes.statement: For any $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q=c^2/\chi_n^{\alpha}(c) <\frac{3}{17}$, we have $\theta_{\alpha}(S(x))$ is increasing on $ [0.1]$.\\

nodes.name: Proof of the monotonicity of $\theta_{\alpha}\circ S$
nodes.statement: We use the notation $u=1-x^2$ and with straightforward computations, we have \begin{eqnarray*} (\theta_{\alpha}(S(x)))'&=&(\theta_{0}(S(x)))'+\frac{2x}{(1-qx^2)^2(1-x^2)^2}\left[q\alpha(\alpha+1)(1-x^2)^2 -q\alpha^2(1-x^2)-\alpha^2(1-qx^2)\right] \\ &=& \frac{2xH(u)}{4u^2(1-q+qu)^4} \end{eqnarray*} where \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &=& G(u)+4(1-q+qu^2)^2[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]\\ &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2[G(u)+4[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]] \end{eqnarray*} with $G(u)\geq\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))\geq0,\;\;\forall q>0,\;\;\alpha>0$ then \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[ \frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))+4[-q\frac{\alpha^3}{\alpha+1}-(1-q)\alpha^2]\right] \\ &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2\left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)u\right]. \end{eqnarray*} Then if $0\leq q\leq\frac{3}{17}$ and $\alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2 \left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)\right]\nonumber\\ &\geq &(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(1+13q)-4\alpha^2\right]\geq0 \end{eqnarray*} $\qquad \Box $
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $u=1-x^2$, factor the derivative as $2xH(u)/(4u^2(1-q+qu)^4)$, and bound $H(u)\geq 0$ under $q\leq 3/17$, $\alpha\leq 1/4$.

nodes.name: Substitute $u=1-x^2$ and compute the derivative
nodes.statement: We use the notation $u=1-x^2$ and with straightforward computations, we have \begin{eqnarray*} (\theta_{\alpha}(S(x)))'&=&(\theta_{0}(S(x)))'+\frac{2x}{(1-qx^2)^2(1-x^2)^2}\left[q\alpha(\alpha+1)(1-x^2)^2 -q\alpha^2(1-x^2)-\alpha^2(1-qx^2)\right] \\ &=& \frac{2xH(u)}{4u^2(1-q+qu)^4} \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Set $u=1-x^2$ and write $(\theta_\alpha\circ S)'$ as $2xH(u)/(4u^2(1-q+qu)^4)$.

nodes.name: Introduce $H(u)$ and the lower bound via $G(u)$
nodes.statement: where \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &=& G(u)+4(1-q+qu^2)^2[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]\\ &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2[G(u)+4[q(\alpha^2+\alpha)u^2-\alpha^2(1-q+2qu)]] \end{eqnarray*} with $G(u)\geq\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))\geq0,\;\;\forall q>0,\;\;\alpha>0$
nodes.statement_short: Define $H(u)$ and bound it below using the nonnegative quantity $G(u)$.

nodes.name: Chain the lower bounds for $H(u)$
nodes.statement: then \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq&(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[ \frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(4-4q+u(17q-3))+4[-q\frac{\alpha^3}{\alpha+1}-(1-q)\alpha^2]\right] \\ &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2\left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)u\right]. \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Successively lower-bound $H(u)$ by an explicit polynomial in $q$, $\alpha$ and $u$.

nodes.name: Conclude nonnegativity under $q\leq 3/17$ and $\alpha\leq 1/4$
nodes.statement: Then if $0\leq q\leq\frac{3}{17}$ and $\alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ we have \begin{eqnarray*} H(u) &\geq& (1-q+qu^2)^2 \left[(1-q)^3-4\alpha^2(1-q\frac{1}{\alpha+1})+\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(17q-3)\right]\nonumber\\ &\geq &(1-q+qu^2)^2\left[\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(1+13q)-4\alpha^2\right]\geq0 \end{eqnarray*} $\qquad \Box $
nodes.statement_short: Under the hypotheses the bracket reduces to $\frac{(1-q)^2}{4}(1+13q)-4\alpha^2\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Uniform local estimate of the GPSWFs
nodes.statement: For any $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and for any integer $n\in \mathbb N,$ with $0<q=\frac{c^2}{\chi_n^\alpha(c)} <\frac{3}{17}$, we have \begin{equation} \ds{\sup_{x\in[0,1]}}\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-qx^2)}\omega_{\alpha}(x)|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x)|^2\leq|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0)|^2+ \frac{|{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)|^2}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)}= A^2 \leq 2 \alpha + 1 \; \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The weighted sup of $|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}|^2$ on $[0,1]$ is bounded by $A^2\leq 2\alpha+1$.
assumptions: For any $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and for any integer $n\in \mathbb N,$ with $0<q=\frac{c^2}{\chi_n^\alpha(c)} <\frac{3}{17}$

nodes.name: Proof of the uniform local estimate
nodes.statement: For $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$ ,we have $ \theta_{\alpha} \circ S $ is increasing. Since $S$ is decreasing then $ \theta $ is also decreasing. We define $K(s)= |V(s)|^2 + \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)}|V'(s)|^2 $ By the fact that $K(s)$ and $ \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)} $ has the same monotonicity and $\theta$ is decreasing , we conclude that $ K $ is increasing. Then $$ |V(S(x))|^2 \leq |K(S(x)) | \leq |K(S(0)) | $$ We remark easily that $ V(S(0)) = \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) $ and $ V'(S(0)) ={ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0) $ then we conclude for the first inequality of \eqref{estimation}. The second inequality is given later on remark \ref{rq}
nodes.statement_short: Build the energy functional $K(s)=|V|^2+|V'|^2/(\chi_n^{\alpha}+\theta)$, show it is increasing, and evaluate at $S(0)$.

nodes.name: Deduce that $\theta$ is decreasing
nodes.statement: For $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$ ,we have $ \theta_{\alpha} \circ S $ is increasing. Since $S$ is decreasing then $ \theta $ is also decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: From the previous lemma and the decrease of $S$, conclude $\theta$ is decreasing.

nodes.name: Introduce the energy functional $K(s)$
nodes.statement: We define $K(s)= |V(s)|^2 + \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)}|V'(s)|^2 $
nodes.statement_short: Define $K(s)=|V(s)|^2+|V'(s)|^2/(\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s))$.

nodes.name: Show $K$ is increasing and bound $|V(S(x))|^2$
nodes.statement: By the fact that $K(s)$ and $ \frac{1}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)+\theta(s)} $ has the same monotonicity and $\theta$ is decreasing , we conclude that $ K $ is increasing. Then $$ |V(S(x))|^2 \leq |K(S(x)) | \leq |K(S(0)) | $$
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $K$ gives $|V(S(x))|^2\leq |K(S(0))|$.

nodes.name: Evaluate at $S(0)$ and conclude
nodes.statement: We remark easily that $ V(S(0)) = \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) $ and $ V'(S(0)) ={ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0) $ then we conclude for the first inequality of \eqref{estimation}. The second inequality is given later on remark \ref{rq}
nodes.statement_short: Identify $V(S(0))$ and $V'(S(0))$ with $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0)$ and its derivative to get the first inequality.

nodes.name: Lower and upper bounds for the eigenvalues $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$
nodes.statement: For c and n such that $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$, we have : \begin{equation} n(n+2\alpha+1)+C_\alpha c^2 \leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) \leq n(n+2\alpha+1)+c^2 \end{equation} Where $$ C_{\alpha} = 2(2\alpha+1)^2+1 - 2(2\alpha+1)\sqrt{1+(2\alpha+1)^2}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Sharpens the classical bounds to $n(n+2\alpha+1)+C_\alpha c^2\leq\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)\leq n(n+2\alpha+1)+c^2$.
assumptions: For c and n such that $0\leq \alpha\leq \frac{1}{4}$ and $0<q<\frac{3}{17}$

nodes.name: Proof of the bounds for $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$
nodes.statement: By differentiating with respect to $c$ the differential equation satisfied by GPSWFs , one gets $$ (1-x^2) \partial_c {{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'}'(x) - 2(\alpha+1)x \partial_c {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(x) + (\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-c^2x^2) \partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$ Hence, we have $$ \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$ It's well known that $\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c $ is a self-adjoint operator and have $ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ as eigenfunctions . Hence, we have $$ < \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}; \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}>_{\omega_{\alpha}} = 0 $$ It follows that $$ \int_{-1}^{1} \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}} ^{2}(x) dx = 0. $$ From the fact that $ \norm{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} = 1 $, one gets \begin{equation} \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) = 2c \int_{-1}^{1} x^2 {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \end{equation} As it is done in \cite{Bonami-Karoui1}, we denote by $ A= \Bigg[\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) + \frac{{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)} \Bigg]^{1/2} $ and consider the auxiliary function $$ K_n(t) = - (1-t^2)^{2\alpha+1} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2 - \frac{(1-t^2)^{2\alpha+2}}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)(1-qt^2)}({\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}')^2 $$ Straightforward computations give us $$ K'_n(t) = 2(2\alpha+1)t(1-t^2)^{2\alpha} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) - {H(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(t)}^2 $$ with $ H(t) \geq 0 $ for $t\in[0,1]$. Hence $$ K'_n(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}^2(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t). $$ So one has the inequality \begin{equation} K_n(1) - K_n(0) = A^2 \leq 2(2\alpha+1) \int_{0}^{1} t{|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |}^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \leq (2\alpha+1) \Bigg[\int_{-1}^{1}t^2 |\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \Bigg] ^{1/2}. \end{equation} That is \begin{equation} A^2 \leq (2\alpha+1) B^{1/2}. \end{equation} Remark that \eqref{estimation} implies that \begin{equation} 1-B \leq 2 A^2 \end{equation} By combining \eqref{11} and \eqref{12} we conclude that $B^{1/2} $ is bounded below by the largest solution of the equation $ X^2 + 2(2\alpha+1) X -1 = 0 $
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the ODE in $c$, use self-adjointness to get $\partial_c\chi_n^{\alpha}$, then bound $B$ via the auxiliary function $K_n$ and a quadratic inequality.

nodes.name: Differentiate the GPSWF ODE with respect to $c$
nodes.statement: By differentiating with respect to $c$ the differential equation satisfied by GPSWFs , one gets $$ (1-x^2) \partial_c {{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'}'(x) - 2(\alpha+1)x \partial_c {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(x) + (\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-c^2x^2) \partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$
nodes.statement_short: Differentiating the defining ODE in $c$ produces an inhomogeneous equation for $\partial_c\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$.

nodes.name: Rewrite in operator form
nodes.statement: Hence, we have $$ \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)} + \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(x) = 0 $$
nodes.statement_short: Recast the differentiated equation as $(\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}+\chi_n^{\alpha}Id)\partial_c\psi+(\partial_c\chi_n^{\alpha}-2cx^2)\psi=0$.

nodes.name: Pair with $\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ using self-adjointness
nodes.statement: It's well known that $\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c $ is a self-adjoint operator and have $ \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}$ as eigenfunctions . Hence, we have $$ < \Big(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c + \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)Id\Big).\partial_c \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}; \psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}>_{\omega_{\alpha}} = 0 $$
nodes.statement_short: Self-adjointness of $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ kills the first term in the inner product.

nodes.name: Derive the formula for $\partial_c\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$
nodes.statement: It follows that $$ \int_{-1}^{1} \Big( \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)-2cx^2 \Big) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}} ^{2}(x) dx = 0. $$ From the fact that $ \norm{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} = 1 $, one gets \begin{equation} \partial_c \chi_n^{\alpha}(c) = 2c \int_{-1}^{1} x^2 {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Obtain $\partial_c\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)=2c\int x^2\psi^2\omega_\alpha$ from the normalization.

nodes.name: Introduce $A$ and the auxiliary function $K_n$
nodes.statement: As it is done in \cite{Bonami-Karoui1}, we denote by $ A= \Bigg[\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(0) + \frac{{\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(0)}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)} \Bigg]^{1/2} $ and consider the auxiliary function $$ K_n(t) = - (1-t^2)^{2\alpha+1} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2 - \frac{(1-t^2)^{2\alpha+2}}{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)(1-qt^2)}({\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}')^2 $$ Straightforward computations give us $$ K'_n(t) = 2(2\alpha+1)t(1-t^2)^{2\alpha} {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) - {H(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}'(t)}^2 $$ with $ H(t) \geq 0 $ for $t\in[0,1]$. Hence $$ K'_n(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}^2(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t) \leq 2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_{\alpha}(t) {\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}}^2(t). $$
nodes.statement_short: Define $A$ and $K_n(t)$ and compute $K_n'(t)$, which is bounded by $2(2\alpha+1)t\omega_\alpha\psi^2$.

nodes.name: Integrate to bound $A^2$ by $(2\alpha+1)B^{1/2}$
nodes.statement: So one has the inequality \begin{equation} K_n(1) - K_n(0) = A^2 \leq 2(2\alpha+1) \int_{0}^{1} t{|\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |}^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \leq (2\alpha+1) \Bigg[\int_{-1}^{1}t^2 |\psi_{n,c}^{(\alpha)}(t) |^2 \omega_{\alpha}(t) dt \Bigg] ^{1/2}. \end{equation} That is \begin{equation} A^2 \leq (2\alpha+1) B^{1/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integrating $K_n'$ over $[0,1]$ yields $A^2\leq(2\alpha+1)B^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Combine with the local estimate and solve the quadratic
nodes.statement: Remark that \eqref{estimation} implies that \begin{equation} 1-B \leq 2 A^2 \end{equation} By combining \eqref{11} and \eqref{12} we conclude that $B^{1/2} $ is bounded below by the largest solution of the equation $ X^2 + 2(2\alpha+1) X -1 = 0 $
nodes.statement_short: Combining with $1-B\leq 2A^2$ bounds $B^{1/2}$ below by the largest root of $X^2+2(2\alpha+1)X-1=0$.

nodes.name: Remark on the bound $A^2\leq 2\alpha+1$
nodes.statement: By using \eqref{11} and since $B\leq1$, one concludes that the constant $A,$ given in \eqref{estimation} satisfies $A^2\leq 2\alpha+1.$

nodes.name: Weighted Sobolev space $\widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}(I)$ associated with $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: by considering the weighted Sobolev space associated with the differential operator defined by $$ \widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}(I) = \{ f\in L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}): \|f\|_{\widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}(I)} = \|(\mathcal{L}^{(\alpha)}_c)^{r/2}.f\|^2 = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(\chi_n^{\alpha})^r |f_k|^2 <\infty \} $$ where $f_k$ are expansions coefficients of $f$ in the GPSWFs's basis.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Wang & Zhang's GPSWFs approximation estimate in $\widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}(I)$
nodes.statement: for any $f \in \widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}(I) $ with $ r\geq 0 $ $$ \| S_{N}.f-f \|_{L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha})} \leq \Big( \chi^{(\alpha)}_{N+1} \Big)^{-r/2} \|f\|_{\widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}(I)} $$
nodes.statement_short: The truncation error is bounded by $(\chi^{(\alpha)}_{N+1})^{-r/2}$ times the $\widetilde H^r$ norm.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Remark comparing the $\widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}$ and $H^r_{\alpha}$ norms
nodes.statement: We have the following norm's comparison given in \cite{Wang2} : $$ \|f\|_{\widetilde{H}^{r}_{\omega_{\alpha}}(I)} \leq C (1+c^2)^{r/2} \|f\|_{r,\omega} $$ Note that for large value of $N$ , we have the same decay rate but when $N^2$ and $ 1+c^2$ are comparable we can notice clearly the importance of the following result.
nodes.statement_short: The two norms give the same decay for large $N$, but the present result is sharper when $N^2$ and $1+c^2$ are comparable.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Approximation of $f\in H^m_{\alpha}(I)$ by the truncated GPSWFs expansion
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \geq 0 $ . For any real number $m \geq 0 $, $ f \in H^m_{\alpha} (I) $ and for any integer number $N \geq 1 $, we have \begin{equation} \norm{f-S_Nf}^2_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} \leq C \Bigg[ \sum_{n=N+1}^{\infty} \Big( \chi_{n}^{(\alpha)} \Big)^{-2m} \Bigg] \norm{f}_{m+2,\alpha}^2 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The squared truncation error is controlled by the tail $\sum_{n>N}(\chi_n^{(\alpha)})^{-2m}$ times $\|f\|^2_{m+2,\alpha}$.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces
assumptions: For any real number $m \geq 0 $, $ f \in H^m_{\alpha} (I) $

nodes.name: Proof of the $H^m_{\alpha}$ approximation theorem
nodes.statement_short: Show $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ is continuous from $H^{r+2}_{\alpha,0}$ to $H^r_{\alpha,0}$, iterate self-adjointness to gain $(\chi_n^{(\alpha)})^{-r}$ per coefficient, then sum the tail and conclude by density and interpolation.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Recall the differential operator $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$
nodes.statement: We recall here the expression of the differential operator $ \mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}$ : $$ \mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)} (f)(x)= -\frac{1}{\omega_{\alpha}(x)} \frac{d}{dx}\left[ \omega_{\alpha}(x) (1-x^2) f'(x)\right] +c^2 x^2 f(x) = -(1-x^2)f''(x) + 2(\alpha+1)xf'(x) + c^2x^2f(x) .$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ in expanded second-order form.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Compute the $r$-th derivative of $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}f$
nodes.statement: For any positive integer $r$ and function $ f\in H^r_{\alpha,0}$ , the derivatives of $ \mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}.f$ are given by : \begin{eqnarray} \frac{d^r}{dx^r}[\mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}.f](x) &=& -(1-x^2) \frac{d^{r+2}f}{dx^{r+2}}(x) + 2(r+\alpha+1)x\frac{d^{r+1}f}{dx^{r+1}}(x) + \Big[ r(2\alpha + r +1)+c^2 x^2 \Big] \frac{d^{r}f}{dx^{r}}(x) \nonumber \\ &+& 2 c^2rx \frac{d^{r-1}f}{dx^{r-1}}(x) + c^2 r(r-1) \frac{d^{r-2}f}{dx^{r-2}}(x) \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Leibniz expansion of $\frac{d^r}{dx^r}[\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}f]$ into five explicit terms.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Deduce the norm bound $\|\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}f\|_{\alpha,r}\leq C\|f\|_{\alpha,r+2}$
nodes.statement_short: Summing the derivative terms gives continuity of $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ between the Sobolev scales.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Iterate by induction on $r$
nodes.statement: Therefore $\mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}$ is a continuous operator from $ H^{r+2}_{\alpha,0}(I)$ into $ H^r_{\alpha,0}(I)$. \\ Then, by induction on $ r $, we obtain \begin{equation} \norm{\Big[\mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}\Big]^r.f}_{\alpha,s} \leq C \norm{f}_{\alpha,r+2} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $r$ extends the bound to powers $[\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}]^r$.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Expand $f$ in the GPSWFs basis
nodes.statement: For $ f \in H^r_{\alpha}(I) $, we write : $$ f = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \hat{f_n}\psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c} \quad \mbox{with} \quad \hat{f_n} = \int_{-1}^1 f(x) \psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) $$
nodes.statement_short: Write $f=\sum_n\hat f_n\psi^{(\alpha)}_{n,c}$ with the weighted coefficients $\hat f_n$.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Move powers of $\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}$ onto $f$ by self-adjointness
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}$ is self adjoint on $L^2(I,\omega_{\alpha}) $, \begin{eqnarray} \hat{f_n} &=& \frac{1}{\chi_{n,\alpha}}\int_{-1}^1 \mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}.\ps(x) f(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx = \frac{1}{\chi_{n,\alpha}}\int_{-1}^1 \mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}.f(x) \ps(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \nonumber \\ &=& ... = \frac{1}{(\chi_{n,\alpha})^r}\int_{-1}^1 \Big[\mathcal{L}_c^{(\alpha)}\Big]^r.f(x) \ps(x) \omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \end{eqnarray}
nodes.statement_short: Repeated self-adjointness gives $\hat f_n=(\chi_{n,\alpha})^{-r}\langle[\mathcal L_c^{(\alpha)}]^rf,\psi\rangle$.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Bound the coefficients
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz plus the operator bound yields $|\hat f_n|^2\leq C(\chi_n^{(\alpha)})^{-2r}\|f\|^2_{r+2,\alpha}$.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Sum the tail, then conclude by density and interpolation
nodes.statement: By writing $ \norm{f-S_Nf}^2_{L^2(I,\omega_\alpha)} = \displaystyle \sum_{n=N+1}^{\infty} |\hat{f_n}|^2 $ one gets \eqref{approx1} Then, we obtain the result for $u$ regular, then for $ u \in H^{r+2}_{\alpha} (I)$ by density and continuity. Finally, for $s$ between two even integers, we conclude by interpolation.
nodes.statement_short: Sum over $n>N$ to get the claim, then extend by density and interpolation to real $s$.
nodes.section: 4 Approximation by the GPSWFs in Weighted Sobolev spaces

nodes.name: Bound on the Jacobi expansion coefficients $|\beta_k^n|$
nodes.statement: In the following, we recall from \cite{Karoui-Souabni1} that for $c > 0$ a fixed positive real number, then, for all positive integers $n,\; k$ such that $q=c^2/\chi^{\alpha}_{n}(c) <1$ and $ k(k+2\alpha+1)+C'_{\alpha}c^2\leq \chi_n^{\alpha}(c)$ , we have \begin{eqnarray} |\beta_k^n|&\leq& C_{\alpha}\left(\frac{2\sqrt{\chi_{n}^{\alpha}(c)}}{c} \right)^k |\mu_{n}^{\alpha}(c)|. \end{eqnarray} With $C'_{\alpha}$ a constant depends only on $\alpha$, and $ {\displaystyle C_{\alpha}=\frac{2^{\alpha}(3/2)^{3/4}(3/2+2\alpha)^{3/4+\alpha}}{e^{2\alpha+3/2}}}$
nodes.statement_short: $|\beta_k^n|\leq C_\alpha(2\sqrt{\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)}/c)^k|\mu_n^{\alpha}(c)|$ under the stated compatibility conditions.

nodes.statement: Let $c>1$ and $\alpha >0$, then for all positive integers $n,\; k$ such that, $k\leq n/1.9$ and $n\geq m_{\alpha}c$ with $m_{\alpha}=4.13\left(1.28+\frac{2\alpha+1}{1.9}\right)^{0.55}$ we have \begin{eqnarray} |\beta_k^n| &\leq & C_{c,\alpha}e^{-\delta n} \end{eqnarray} with $\delta$ and $C_{c,\alpha}$ positive constants .
nodes.statement_short: For $k\leq n/1.9$ and $n\geq m_\alpha c$, the coefficients satisfy $|\beta_k^n|\leq C_{c,\alpha}e^{-\delta n}$.

nodes.name: Insert the eigenvalue bound into the coefficient bound
nodes.statement_short: Combine $(\ref{9})$, $(\ref{Eq3.1})$ and $\chi_n^{\alpha}(c)\leq n(n+2\alpha+1)+c^2$ into a chain of estimates.

nodes.name: Example 2: GPSWFs approximation of a Brownian motion function
nodes.statement: {\bf Example 2:} In this example, for a positive real number $s$, we consider the Brownian motion function $$ B_s(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{X_k}{k^s} \cos(k \pi x) \quad x\in I=[-1,1] $$ Here $X_k$ is a sequence of independent standard Gaussian random variable. It is well known that $B_s\in H^{s'-1/2}(I),$ for any $s'< s-\frac{1}{2}.$ Here, $H^s(I)$ is the Sobolev space over $I,$ with smoothness exponent $s.$ For the special values of $s=1.5$ and $ c= 5\pi $, and the two values of $N=46$ and $N=90,$ we have computed $S_N(B_s),$ the truncated series expansion to the order $N,$ of $B_s$ in the GPSWFs basis. We have found that $$\| B_s - S_{46}(B_s)\|_{\infty} \approx 01 E-01,\qquad \| B_s - S_{90}(B_s)\|_{\infty} \approx 05 E-02.$$ Moreover, the graphs of $B_{s}$ and of its approximation $S_{90} B_{s}$ are given by the figure \ref{brownian}.
nodes.statement_short: Approximates a random Fourier-series Brownian path $B_s$ by its GPSWFs truncations at $N=46$ and $N=90$.

For this purpose, we have computed the different expansion coefficients $ \displaystyle{ C_n(M_{s,\lambda}(x)) = \int_{-1}^{1}M_{s,\lambda}(x)\ps(y) \omega_{\alpha}(y)dy }$ which are exactly given thanks to \eqref{Eq3.2}. Since $M_{s,\lambda}$ is an odd function , $C_{2n}(M_{s,\lambda}) = $ . Moreover \begin{eqnarray} C_{2n+1}(M_{s,\lambda}) &=& \sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}\beta_{2\ell+1}^{2m+1} \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{\lambda^{k(2-s)}} \int_{-1}^{1} \sin(\lambda^k x) \hat{P}^{(\alpha)}_{2\ell+1}(x)\omega_{\alpha}(x) dx \nonumber \\ &=& \sqrt{\pi} 2^{\alpha+\frac{1}{2}} \sum_{\ell=1}^{\infty} (-1)^{\ell} \beta_{2\ell+1}^{2m+1} \frac{\Gamma(2\ell+\alpha+3)}{\sqrt(h_{2\ell+1})\Gamma(2\ell+1)} \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \lambda^{k(s-\alpha-5/2)} J_{2\ell + \alpha+\frac{3}{2}}(\lambda^k) \end{eqnarray} In figure \ref{WM} we have plotted the function $M_{1,2}$ and the graph of the error $ M_{1,2} - S_N(M_{1,2}(x)) $
